title: Trust Receipt v0 (dev.trustshell.trust-receipt/0.1-draft). DESIGN DRAFT: not implemented, not ratified, not part of 1.8.0
description: One host-independent record that keeps six things apart: what was INTENDED, what was AUTHORIZED (and under which authority mode), what was EXECUTED (as the executor reports it), what was OBSERVED (dev.trustshell.action-evidence records, never a second evidence format), what is UNKNOWN (first-class entries, never omitted), and PROVENANCE (one label per part, plus the receipt's own digest and signature). A part that was not recorded is null AND has a NOT_RECORDED entry in `unknown`. A receipt that passes this schema is well-formed, NOT valid: a verifier must still recompute every digest, verify every signature, and resolve every `ref`. See docs/trust-receipt.md.

digest.description: Over `receipt`. Shows the receipt is unchanged compared with a copy of this value obtained elsewhere. Carried in the same file, it catches only accidental damage. It names no one.

signature.description: null = nobody signed the receipt. Required so that 'not signed' is stated, never left out.

assembled_by.description: What put the parts together. Stated: authenticated only by a verified receipt `signature`.

unknown.description: Never empty: an empty list cannot be told apart from a producer that forgot.

payment.description: RESERVED. Always null in v0. A payment part will need four explicit bindings before it can mean anything: the exact deliverable, the acceptance criteria, the beneficiary or counterparty, and independent outcome evidence. A SUPPORTED CI-run claim is none of these.

statement.description: What the agent was asked to accomplish, as the requester put it.

mode.description: Required, no default, so the mode is always named and never implied. LOCAL_GUARDRAIL: owner-editable; anyone who can act as the owner can change it, and it binds only the paths it mediates. PROTECTED_OWNER_AUTHORITY: verified by an enforcement component the agent cannot rewrite. No TrustShell component emits PROTECTED_OWNER_AUTHORITY today.

permits.description: What the owner permitted, in the policy's own terms (for Guard: its `actions` entries and limits).

enforcer.description: The component that enforced the policy, if one did.

provenance.description: `digest` is the policy's own digest; `signature`, if any, is over the policy. A signature names the key that signed; it never makes the mode PROTECTED.

then.description: Necessary, not sufficient: v0 has no way to carry evidence that the agent cannot rewrite the enforcer (docs/trust-receipt.md, open question 2).

executor.description: Which executor reported. null when it was not recorded; then `unknown` says so.

statements.description: What the executor reports happened, in its own words. A report, never a finding: findings live in `observed`.

kind.description: The one evidence format. No competing format: a new source of evidence becomes a new observation platform or template inside action-evidence.

carriage.description: EMBEDDED: the record is in this receipt and can be checked offline against `provenance.digest`. REFERENCED: only a pointer and a digest are here; checking it needs the record from elsewhere, so offline it is NOT_CHECKED.

origin.description: action-evidence/0.1-draft records are a platform reporting on its own run; an assembler may not relabel them.

integrity.description: Every action-evidence record has a digest.

actionEvidenceRecord.description: The members of a dev.trustshell.action-evidence/0.1-draft record this contract depends on. src/lib/action-evidence.ts stays the authority for the rest; this does not redefine it.

fetchedAt.description: When the platform was read. LIVE means live at this moment; read later, the record is a snapshot of it.

status.description: Three outcomes, never two. NOT_CHECKED is never a pass.

kind.description: NOT_RECORDED: nobody wrote it down. NOT_CHECKED: recorded, but no evidence here decides it. INACCESSIBLE: the evidence exists and could not be read. OUTSIDE_OBSERVATION: nothing that made this receipt could have seen it.

ref.description: RFC 6901 pointer into this document (from its root, so it starts /receipt/...), or null. Points at the gap instead of copying it.

source.description: Where the part came from, as stated. Unauthenticated unless `integrity` is SIGNED and the reader verifies the signature.

origin.description: Who is speaking. STATED: a party said it. SELF_REPORTED: an actor about its own action. PLATFORM_REPORTED: a platform about its own records. INDEPENDENT: re-derived by an observer neither the actor nor the platform controls; nothing emits it in v0.

integrity.description: A digest is not a signature. DIGEST_ONLY: the content can be compared with this digest; it names no one. SIGNED: a signature over the content is carried with its public key; only once a reader verifies it does it name a key, and a key is never a person.

digest.description: Computed by the part's source over the part's own content, not by the assembler.

verifier.description: The tool, and its version, that produced or checked this part. null or a null version is a gap to list in `unknown`.

digest.description: The shape of src/lib/action-evidence.ts RecordDigest: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical form.

signature.description: The shape of Guard's policy signature (src/lib/guardrails.ts PolicySignature): Ed25519 over the RFC 8785 bytes the digest hashes, base64. It names a key, never a person, and only after it verifies.
